decision: Workspaces show within 1 second of Winland starting and clear within 1 second of it stopping, whichever starts first
why: The bar stays empty until the next look, and a shell that has been up can be 30 seconds from that look

decision: Scope is the Winland look loop, one services test, and one omarchy inspect run. The user's Winland on pipe winland-1 stays up
why: A second Winland is safe only on its own pipe, with a config that ignores every window

decision: Rigor stays on one mechanism. No second design. The 3 to 30 second schedule is the suspect, and the widget already hides when ProcessId is 0
why: PR 626 lengthened the look so an all-day poll would wake the CPU less often

decision: A connect to a missing pipe took 271 ms and about 37 ms of CPU. File.Exists on the pipe path took 0.3 ms and saw winland-1
why: The backoff was hiding an expensive probe. A cheap exists check can run several times a second
result: probe is File.Exists, look is 250 ms

decision: The arrival test timed out while the shell was already looking. The same peer showed workspaces when the pipe was already there
why: The 3 second wait is the delay. The pipe server itself answers
evidence: dotnet test WinlandArrivalTests, failed then the already-running fact passed

decision: Look with File.Exists and wait 250 ms, including after a dropped stream. Skip Connect until the pipe is there
why: A missing-pipe Connect costs about 37 ms of CPU, so the old backoff was paying for the probe

decision: Six runs showed workspaces in 57 to 137 ms and cleared them in 9 to 17 ms. Winland already running showed them in 31 to 32 ms
why: The 1 second bound has room. The spread sits inside the 250 ms look

decision: With the omarchy bar already up, Workspace 1 was in the tree 815 ms after the private Winland answered, and gone 742 ms after it stopped
why: Each figure is the time until inspect returned, so the bar changed at or before that. The user's Winland on pid 23528 stayed up

decision: When Winland was already answering, the first tree read after the bar was ready contained Workspace 1. That read returned 4030 ms after the shell process started and about 1.6 s after Ready
why: The 4030 ms includes WinUI startup and one inspect call. It is not an empty bar waiting on the old 3 to 30 second look
